([[Chandler, Arizona]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * Second-team All SEC (2022) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2022) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) | medal_templates = }} '''Tyrone "TyTy" Washington Jr.''' (born November 15, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. ==High school career== Washington played basketball for [[Cesar Chavez High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|Cesar Chavez High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 23.2 points, 4.1 assists, 4.4 rebounds and 3.3 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Obert |first1=Richard |title=TyTy Washington ready to make hoops history at Cesar Chavez |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/11/14/tyty-washington-ready-make-hoops-history-cesar-chavez/4195597002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=November 14, 2019}} Washington transferred to AZ Compass Prep School in [[Chandler, Arizona]] during his junior season.{{cite web |last1=Obert |first1=Richard |title=Cesar Chavez hoops moves on without star TyTy Washington, routs Tempe |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/26/chavez-moves-without-star-washington-rout-tempe/2752449001/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=December 26, 2019}} As a senior, he averaged 24 points, seven assists and six rebounds per game, leading his team to a 30–2 record.{{cite web |last1=Tucker |first1=Kyle |title=After his decommitment from Creighton, TyTy Washington is blowing up — and could head to Kentucky |url=https://theathletic.com/2520093/2021/04/14/after-his-decommitment-from-creighton-tyty-washington-is-blowing-up-and-could-head-to-kentucky/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021}} He was named to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |last1=Lindsey |first1=Eric |title=Three UK MBB Signees Selected to Jordan Brand Classic Roster |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2021/5/23/mens-basketball-three-uk-mbb-signees-selected-to-jordan-brand-classic-roster |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=May 23, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Washington was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. On November 15, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |last1=Nyatawa |first1=Jon |title=Four-star guard TyTy Washington commits to Creighton |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/four-star-guard-tyty-washington-commits-to-creighton/article_e7272b4b-e4ea-510f-882d-7348e2b66a68.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=November 15, 2020}} He decommitted on March 11, 2021, nine days after head coach [[Greg McDermott]] recalled telling his players, "I need everybody to stay on the plantation. I can't have anybody leave the plantation," following a loss in February.{{cite web |last1=Boren |first1=Cindy |title=Creighton loses a prized recruit over Coach Greg McDermott's plantation comment |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/15/greg-mcdermott-tyty-washington-plantation/ |website=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=April 15, 2021}} On May 12, 2021, Washington committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Five-star point guard TyTy Washington commits to Kentucky Wildcats |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31435285/five-star-point-guard-tyty-washington-commits-kentucky-wildcats |website=[[ESPN]] He was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as well as the All Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} On April 6, 2022, Washington declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Kentucky freshman guard TyTy Washington Jr. entering NBA draft, plans to hire agent|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33683968/kentucky-freshman-guard-tyty-washington-jr-entering-nba-draft-plans-hire-agent|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|date=April 6, 2022|accessdate=April 6, 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] | 31 || 29 || 29.2 || .451 || .350 || .750 || 3.5 || 3.9 || 1.3 || .2 || 12.5 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ukathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyty-washington/9335 Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Washington, TyTy}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Phoenix, Arizona]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]]
